_comment: Source: /tmp/Risk Modeling Exercise Synthesis Agent Questions.txt (from boss, 2026-05-21). Each question is tagged with scope (per-submission or cross-submission). For per-submission questions, 'answers_from' lists the rubric question IDs (prefix s= Science rubric, p= Practitioner rubric) whose answers compose the response. answer_kind: 'direct' = pull values from one rubric field; 'synthesized' = compose paragraph from multiple fields; 'no_rubric_basis' = requires analytical inference we did not perform (mark as requires_reviewer_judgment).

questions.text: What external/additional data did the model utilize beyond the provided exercise data?
How many submissions used additional inputs beyond what's contained in the synthetic data?
What external data inputs were used that were not from the synthetic data provided?
What are the sources for these external data inputs?
Are there any trends or patterns in the type or category of external data inputs used?
If fuel treatment/management data was used, which ones?
Were there common additional inputs? What are the clusters of those?
How do the fuel moisture content and vegetation type distributions differ spatially between the two study locations?
Compare model outputs (general comparison)
How do the predicted outputs compare across all submissions in terms of burned area extent, spatial pattern, and intensity distribution?
What is the spatial overlap between burned area polygons predicted by different models at each location?
How does the variance in predicted fire perimeter size compare across models within each location, and is that variance consistent between the two locations?
Are the outputs tailored to different user communities or are they general?
What are the clusters of modeling approaches for fire behavior?
What areas of commonality are models sharing knowledge in?
How do the predicted rate-of-spread values differ spatially across models, and where do the largest disagreements occur within each location?
In the town of forests, do the fire modeling approaches take into account crown and surface fire behavior?
What are the workflow patterns in each submission?
How similar are the workflow patterns?
Which components of risk does the model include: Hazard, Exposure, Vulnerability, Structure-to-Structure, etc.?
Does the workflow account for transparency and provenance of the data and models it uses?
What are the dominant workflow patterns identified in this submission (e.g., data prep → simulation → post-processing)?
How modular is the workflow — can individual components be swapped out or updated independently?
Is the workflow designed for a one-time analysis or repeated operational runs?
Does the workflow produce intermediate outputs that can be independently checked or audited?
What common data preparation steps did teams use to make data ready for analysis?
What metrics did the team utilize to benchmark and validate their model?

sections.name: Fitness for Practical Use and Operational Relevance

questions.text: What wildfire risk problem is the submission actually solving?
Who is the intended user (incident command, utility, planners, insurers, prescribed fire managers, community resilience planners, etc.)?
What operational decisions does the model support?
Is the model spatial and temporal resolution appropriate for the intended use?
Is it realistic for practitioners to use this approach for decision support?
What assumptions, if any, would limit the use of the approach in practical settings?
Does the model account for and quantify its uncertainty?
Can this model be used for predictive analytics? How susceptible is the model to dataset shift?

sections.name: Risk Modeling Definition and Decision Support

questions.text: How is "risk" defined? Is the definition based on the value of potential loss/damage, probability of loss, or vulnerability to loss?

Does the workflow distinguish hazard, exposure, vulnerability, and consequence? If exposure is distinguished, which mechanisms (radiation, convection, ember transport) are included? How sensitive are these mechanisms to the variables in the data?
Are cascading or compound risks represented?
Can the approach incorporate or interoperate with existing models and datasets?
For the same model run across both locations, how does spatial accuracy of burned area prediction change, and what landscape variables best explain that difference?
Across all models and both locations, which combination shows the greatest spatial agreement in fire behavior outputs, and what input conditions drive that consensus?
What common gaps appear across the submissions?
Which submissions represent currently operational capabilities vs emerging science-based approaches?
